newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanjin Heavy out of court receivership.
newsitem.headline: Hanjin Heavy out of court receivership.

text.p: Hanjin Heavy Industry, a debt-ridden shipbuilding unit of South Korea's Hanjin Group, said on Monday it had emerged from court receivership as its business was back to normal.
A Hanjin Heavy official said the company had been under court receivership for seven years.
Brokers said the move was widely anticipated, given the profits Hanjin Heavy had reported in the past several years.

After the Hanjin Group took over the state-funded Korea Shipping and Engineering Corp in 1989, it changed the firm's name to Hanjin Heavy. But a prolonged slump in domestic shipubilding industry and Korea Shipping's large debts put the company under court receivership and its shares on the supervision list on the Seoul bourse.
"Our efforts to normalise business are paying off," a Hanjin spokesman said.
He added brisk sales of higher-value added products including liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers and high-speed railway trains also contributed to the company's profits.
The Korea Stock Exchange suspended trading in the shares of Hanjin Heavy for Monday's afternoon trading. Trading will resume on Tuesday in the second-tier section.
The shares last traded at 7,790 won, up 100 won, before being suspended.
